mcat_description.short: Mobile Toilet Van is a trailer-mounted or chassis-mounted multi-seat portable sanitation unit fabricated in MS or FRP, sold as a complete assembly with integrated fresh water tank, sludge/waste tank, and plumbing fittings for deployment at public events, construction sites, and municipal sanitation programs.
mcat_description.long: Mobile Toilet Vans (MTVs) are factory-fabricated, wheeled sanitation structures built on a trailer chassis or vehicle body, housing 2 to 14 individual toilet/urinal cabins in a single mobile unit. The body is constructed from Mild Steel (MS) channel and angle sections or Fiberglass Reinforced Plastic (FRP), with PVC-coated GI sheet interior panelling, and is fitted with a fresh water tank (500–1,200 litres), a sludge/waste tank, and complete internal plumbing. Waste management options include conventional sludge tanks (requiring periodic pump-out), bio-digester tanks using DRDO-developed anaerobic technology that converts sewage into safe effluent, and chemical toilet systems. MTVs are widely deployed by municipal corporations, Smart City projects, event organizers, construction contractors, and government agencies under the Swachh Bharat Mission, and are available in standard seater configurations (4, 6, 8, 10) as well as customised sizes.

market_context: Mobile Toilet Vans (MTVs) are a well-established product category in the Indian B2B sanitation market, driven primarily by government programs including the Swachh Bharat Mission and Smart City initiatives. The dominant commercial form is a trailer-mounted unit in 4, 6, 8, or 10-seater configurations, fabricated from either Mild Steel (MS) or Fiberglass Reinforced Plastic (FRP); FRP is increasingly preferred for its corrosion resistance and lighter weight. A significant and growing sub-segment is the bio-digester MTV, which uses DRDO-developed anaerobic digestion technology to convert sewage into safe effluent without requiring pump-out infrastructure — this variant is particularly favoured for rural, semi-urban, and remote deployments. Key manufacturing hubs include Ghaziabad (UP), Faridabad (Haryana), New Delhi, Pune, and Ahmedabad. Buyers are predominantly institutional: municipal corporations, urban local bodies, construction contractors, and event management companies. The AC/luxury executive variant is a smaller but distinct sub-segment targeting premium events and corporate CSR deployments. All raw materials are required to conform to Indian Standards (IS/ISO approved makes); transport commissioner design approval is required for road-mobile variants. CPCB environmental compliance governs waste discharge from sludge tanks. The product is sold per piece, with seater count as the primary SKU differentiator.
